discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap concept and its realization in photonic crystal fibers

nominees.name: Philip St.J. Russell
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Erlangen, Germany

motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that a periodic dielectric structure can open a photonic band gap, forbidding light propagation and suppressing spontaneous emission, and that disorder in such media can localize light. Yablonovitch then fabricated the first three-dimensional photonic band-gap crystal. The idea turned the control of light into a matter of engineered wavelength-scale structure, and it underlies modern nanophotonics: high-Q nanocavities, slow light, topological photonics and integrated quantum light sources. Russell carried the concept into optical fiber. His photonic crystal fibers, drawn from stacked glass capillaries using an elegantly simple method, guide light by band-gap and microstructure effects, including in hollow cores. They enabled broadband supercontinuum sources that were essential for self-referenced optical frequency combs and are now standard tools in ultrafast optics, spectroscopy and gas-based nonlinear photonics. Together these contributions turned a fundamental insight into light confinement into a platform used across physics and technology.
